token_is_non_standard.meaning: the underlying asset is a non-standard ERC20 token such as USDT that does not return a boolean on transfer

fees_distributed_in_non_standard_token.meaning: builder fees are distributed in non-standard ERC20 tokens and transferred to the BuilderWallet

token_transfer_succeeds.meaning: the token-level transfer succeeds even though no boolean is returned

sweep_reverts.meaning: the sweep call reverts despite the transfer succeeding at the token level

claims.scope: BuilderWallet.sweep of protocol-generated builder fees in non-standard ERC20 tokens

preconditions.text: The underlying asset is a non-standard ERC20 token such as USDT that does not return a boolean on transfer.; Builder fees are distributed in such non-standard ERC20 tokens and transferred to the BuilderWallet.; The report assumes the token-level transfer succeeds even though no boolean is returned.
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.

safety.text: Inferred: the sweep function should complete the withdrawal of builder fees for non-standard ERC20 tokens whose transfer succeeds at the token level, rather than reverting on the missing boolean return value.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.

effects.text: The sweep call reverts despite the transfer succeeding at the token level, causing the withdrawal to fail.
effects.derivation: Program-generated direct negation witness for the selected safety pattern.

effect_coverage.reason: Program-generated exact coverage for selected direct impact.

assumptions: The sweep function is called to withdraw the builder fees from the BuilderWallet.
The builder fees are held in the BuilderWallet before the sweep attempt.
The token-level transfer succeeds even though no boolean is returned.

limitations: Only the direct revert impact i_sweep_reverts is formalized; the downstream impact i_fees_inaccessible is deferred to a future claim.
The root cause rc_boolean_assumption is not encoded as a precondition; it is treated as context for the vulnerable behavior.
The scenario is conditional on a non-standard ERC20 being used; no concrete token address or transaction is provided.
The sweep caller identity is unspecified and does not affect the selected progress/liveness relation.
